idea: Objective transit quality indicators: service frequency (runs per hour, average headway), daily service hours, stop spacing, walking distance to stop, travel speed of runs, reliability as runs executed over runs scheduled, punctuality as share of runs on time with on-time defined as up to 1 minute early and up to 5 minutes late (TCRP Report 100), regularity of headways, crowding as load factor (passengers per seat) and standing area; indicators judged against a standard, a past value, an A-F level of service, a ratio or an index combining several. Users value reliability and frequency most; waiting, walking and transfer time are felt more onerous than in-vehicle time.
does: Per bus line from a run: schedule adherence (share within -1 / +5 min of timetable at stops), headway regularity (coefficient of variation of headways, bunching share), average speed, runs completed, and a TSP evaluation comparing these with and without priority.
outputs: on-time share, headway CV, bunching, speed per line; A-F grade
existing: partial: results by vehicle type, TSP wait and passenger delay per trip
cite: Ch 2 (Eboli and Mazzulla), Table 1, Measures based on transit performance
notes: Gives the TSP and DEVL agents a standard outcome measure beyond delay; load factor needs passengers (not built).

idea: Isochronal map of travel-time contours (20, 40, 60, 80 min) from a new town showing which employment centres are reachable, built from route tests that include walking to the station and transfer time; rail and bus give similar total time because of transfers.
does: Draw travel-time contours from a chosen junction, end or institution over the network (shortest time at free flow or from a run), with the institutions and jobs inside each band.
outputs: map overlay, counts of institutions/employees per band
existing: none (critical_links and assign_routes compute route times but no contour)
cite: Ch 3 (Lau), 4.2 Travel Time Route Test, Fig 4

idea: Energy from force balance: motive force F_M = F_g + F_R + F_C with gravity F_g = M g i_s (gradient), running resistance F_R = M(a + bV + cV^2) (internal, rolling, aerodynamic), curve resistance F_C = K/R; with acceleration F_M >= sum; work W = integral of F_M dl counting only positive F_M (consumption), the negative part being the energy that regenerative braking could return; speed limited by the minimum of class, type, infrastructure and curve limits, and by power and maximum tractive effort.
does: Per-vehicle energy use from each simulated trajectory by a road-vehicle version: m*a + rolling + aero drag (+ curve resistance from radius) integrated over positive power, with a regeneration share for electric types; gives kWh or litres per km by vehicle type and per scenario, with no emission tables needed.
inputs: vehicle trajectories (speed, accel), mass, rolling and drag coefficients, regen efficiency
outputs: energy per vehicle, per km, per link, network total
cite: Ch 6 (Lopez et al.), Section 4 Methodology, 4.1 Calculating Consumption
notes: Source is rail (Spain freight); the equation structure transfers, coefficients are the user's. Pairs with link_emissions (Arndt) and emissions_kpis (AgentSUMO).
